newsitem.title: USA: San Diego, Calif., moves closer to vote on stadium.
newsitem.headline: San Diego, Calif., moves closer to vote on stadium.

text.p: San Diego moved a step closer to a public vote on its $78 million stadium expansion plan, directing city attorneys to draft an ordinance calling for the special referendum, officials said on Wednesday.

San Diego's city council asked its attorneys to prepare the ordinance and voted to rescind a December project addendum that added $18 million to the controversial expansion project, Mayor Susan Golding's spokewoman, MaryAnne Pintar, said.
The council will meet again by Feb 10 on the ordinance. The ballot measure could be structured to include just the $18 million additions or the entire Jack Murphy Stadium expansion.
"It is the mayor's intent to hold this election as quickly as possible under the law," Pintar said. "(The month of) May is a possibility."

Earlier this month, the city's clerk announced that petitions seeking a public referendum on the expansion were valid. But the petition review did not settle the dispute between city officials and critics of the expansion plan.

Project opponents maintain that the $18 million of additions substantially changed the original expansion plan. As a result, the entire $78 million expansion project should be placed on the ballot, their attorney, Mike Aguirre, said.
Golding has urged the city council to place only the $18 million addendum on the ballot.
